name: Thick-billed Seed-Finch
rangeDescription: Southern mexico (veracruz) to western colombia and western ecuador; also coiba and pearl islands
description: Small seed-eating bird of humid tropical lowlands; uncommon. Found in damp grassy areas, overgrown weedy fields, and forest edges, often in areas with scattered bushes and small trees.

name: Orange-billed Babbler
rangeDescription: Humid forest of sri lanka
description: A large, uniform rufous-brown babbler with conspicuous orange bill and feet, and a beady yellow eye. Highly gregarious, usually encountered in noisy flocks within wet rainforest understory.

name: Hawaiian Goose
rangeDescription: Upland lava flows of hawaii; introduced to maui
description: A distinctively marked goose with neck feathers that have a peculiar furrowed appearance. Occurs in wetlands, grassy areas, golf courses, montane shrubland, parks, and even lava fields with sparse vegetation.

name: Giant Ibis
rangeDescription: Lowlands of thailand, cambodia, laos, and southern vietnam
description: A hulking gray ibis the size of a large goose and with a distinctively long-bodied appearance, this increasingly rare scimitar-billed waterbird is unmistakable in its limited range. Size alone separates this species from other ibises that share its range; also note wrinkly bald head, dark back, and beautifully scalloped wings.

name: Kipengere Seedeater
rangeDescription: Southern tanzania (mount rungwe and udzungwa mountains)
description: A large seedeater with a big, bulging bill. Dark brown above and white below with heavily streaked underparts.

name: Light-mantled Albatross
rangeDescription: Circumpolar subantarctic islands; ranges north to 35°s
description: A small, dark albatross with pointed wings and tail. Note the ashy-gray neck and back feathers contrasting with the dark head.

name: Abyssinian Catbird
rangeDescription: Highland juniper and hagenia forest of ethiopia
description: An unusual and distinctive warbler of the Ethiopian highlands. Mostly gray with chestnut under the tail, a red eye, black between the eye and bill, and a white patch above the eye.

name: Red-faced Parrot
rangeDescription: Andes of southwestern ecuador and adjacent northwestern peru
description: Rare and threatened parrot found only in high Andean forest in southern Ecuador and adjacent parts of northern Peru. Small compared to most other parrots.

name: Red-backed Mousebird
rangeDescription: Euphorbia savanna of angola; formerly southwestern gabon
description: A brownish-gray dumpy-bodied bird with a long scruffy tail, a reddish back, brown ears, a brown crest, and pale eyes. Occurs in small sociable groups in forest edge, woodland, thorn scrub, and cultivated areas along the Angolan escarpment, where it is endemic.
imageCreditName: Lars Petersson | My World of Bird Photography

name: Kenya Rufous Sparrow
rangeDescription: Kenya and tanzania
description: A typical sparrow with a striped back, a gray crown and nape, and a dark bib. The rufous rump is conspicuous in flight.

name: Orange-throated Tanager
rangeDescription: Río marañón drainage in southeastern ecuador (zamora-chinchipe) and northern peru (northern amazonas)
description: Unique and beautiful rainforest tanager known only from several remote areas of the eastern Andes in northern Peru and southeastern Ecuador. No other Andean bird has an orange throat, black upperparts, and blue wings.

name: Gray-winged Francolin
rangeDescription: Grassland of lesotho and west-central south africa
description: Medium-sized, beautifully-patterned francolin. Shows small rufous patches in the wings in flight.

name: Fine-barred Piculet
rangeDescription: Foothills of eastern peru (loreto to cusco and madre de dios)
description: Small, pale piculet. Light tan below, olive-brown above, with a black-and-white speckled crown; males have a red crown patch.

name: Ecuadorian Tyrannulet
rangeDescription: East slope of andes of eastern ecuador and northern peru (san martín)
description: Small, warbler-like flycatcher found in cloud forest along the east slope of the Andes in Ecuador, northern Peru, and southern Colombia. Plumage is yellow-olive with a gray crown, yellowish wingbars, white eyebrow, and black stripe through the eye.

name: Bali Myna
rangeDescription: Coastal northwestern bali (bali barat national park); extinct in the wild with reintroductions in nusa penida island and (usually unsuccessful) in western bali
description: An eye-catching white starling with black tips to the tail and wings, bare blue facial skin, and long plumes that hang down the nape. Juvenile is shorter-crested than adult, with yellow wash.

name: Hooded Wheatear
rangeDescription: Rocky desert ravines of northeastern sudan and egypt to southern pakistan
description: A pretty wheatear of arid zones. Its long bill and elongated tail and wings give it an elegant silhouette.

name: Tepui Vireo
rangeDescription: Tepuis of southern venezuela, western guyana, and far northern brazil
description: Small, arboreal bird of tepui highlands. Olive-gray above and yellowish below, with a gray head, pinkish bill, and pale eye.

name: Oriental Cuckoo
rangeDescription: Breeds western russia and kazakhstan through northeastern russia to japan; winters southeastern asia, indonesian archipelago, and philippines to northern and eastern australia, new guinea and satellite islands, bismarck archipelago, and solomon islands
description: Typical gray cuckoo, indistinguishable from Himalayan Cuckoo in the field by plumage. Dark bands on the breast average broader in Oriental.

name: Ursula's Sunbird
rangeDescription: Montane forest of mount cameroon and bioko (gulf of guinea)
description: A small, inconspicuous, and easily overlooked sunbird of mountain forests. At a distance, appears fairly uniform in color, but in good light the greenish back contrasts with the gray face, olive throat, pale belly, and reddish tufts on the sides of the body that are sometimes concealed by the wings.

name: Tawny-collared Nightjar
rangeDescription: Tropical eastern mexico (nuevo león to oaxaca and chiapas)
description: Fairly large dark nightjar of woodland, edge, and adjacent clearings in northeast Mexico. Hunts mainly from perches at forest edge, sometimes even on fence posts in rather open areas.
